## Update check

### `sc_wpun_after_update_check`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when an update check has finished, after the state was saved.

It fires even if nothing was sent, with an empty `$results`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | The notification of the check, with every item that was waiting. |
| `$results` | `array<string, Delivery_Result>` | Result by channel instance id, for the instances something was sent to. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_before_update_check`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when an update check starts, before anything is looked up.

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_frequencies`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the names of the cron schedules offered as check frequencies.

Each must be a registered schedule (see the `cron_schedules` filter) of at
least an hour.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$names` | `string[]` | Schedule names. Default hourly, twicedaily, daily and weekly. |

Fired in `includes/class-frequencies.php`.

### `sc_wpun_item_resolved`

*Action*, since 3.0.0

Fires once per channel instance when an update it reported is no longer pending.

The update check compares what each instance was told (its `notified` state) with what is
pending now. An item that was reported and is no longer pending at all is resolved, and is then
forgotten. Use it to close a helpdesk ticket opened from a webhook notification, to log the
time to update (see `Notification_Item::get_notified_at()`), or to post "done" to whatever
received the alert.

`$how` is `updated` when the installed version of a plugin or theme is now the reported version
or newer, `removed` when the plugin or theme is no longer installed, and `core` when WordPress
is at or past the reported version.

The check finds this out, not the install, so it does not matter how the update was installed
(Updates screen, automatic updates, WP-CLI, a host, an uploaded zip or FTP), but it can take up
to one check interval. Only core, plugin and theme items are reported; an item of an add-on type
is forgotten silently. It fires for every instance that reported the item, also one that is
switched off or waiting after a Retry-After (see `Channel_Instance::is_enabled()`), and for an
item recorded when an instance was added with "skip what's waiting".

It does not fire for an item that is muted, snoozed, replaced by a newer version or hidden by the
`sc_wpun_should_notify_item` filter: those are still pending. An update installed while the item
is snoozed is never reported as resolved, because the snooze made the check forget the entry. It
never fires in a dry run or for a test notification. If two checks overlap it can fire twice;
see ADR 0009.

The item is as it was reported: its new version is the one reported, and its name, installed
version and links (without the download link) are from then. Entries stored before 3.0.0 have
no details: the name is the installed one, if there is one, and `get_notified_at()` is null.

Example, log the time to update:

```php
add_action(
    'sc_wpun_item_resolved',
    function ( $item, $how, $instance ) {
        $since = $item->get_notified_at();
        if ( null !== $since ) {
            error_log( sprintf( '%s was %s after %d seconds.', $item->get_name(), $how, time() - $since ) );
        }
    },
    10,
    3
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$item` | `Notification_Item` | The item as it was reported. |
| `$how` | `string` | `updated`, `removed` or `core`. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The channel instance that reported it. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

## Items and routing

### `sc_wpun_channel_should_receive_item`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters whether a channel instance receives an item, for rules of your own.

Runs after the instance's own rules, so it can veto an item the rules let through and
allow one they blocked.

Example, send only plugins named "security" to the instance called "security_team":

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_channel_should_receive_item',
    function ( $receive, $item, $instance ) {
        if ( 'security_team' === $instance->get_id() && 'plugin' === $item->get_type() ) {
            return false !== stripos( $item->get_name(), 'security' );
        }
        return $receive;
    },
    10,
    3
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$receive` | `bool` | Whether the instance receives the item. |
| `$item` | `Notification_Item` | The item. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance. |

Fired in `includes/class-routing.php`.

### `sc_wpun_core_needs_update`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters whether a WordPress core update is reported, like the plugin and theme filters do for theirs.

The default follows the "Notify about WordPress updates?" setting: true, or with "only major
releases" whether the update is a major.minor change. Returning false reports no core item.
What was already notified about core is kept while the update is waiting.

Example, ignore release candidates:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_core_needs_update',
    function ( $needs, $new_version ) {
        return $needs && false === strpos( $new_version, '-RC' );
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$needs` | `bool` | Whether to report the update. Default true, or whether it is a major release with "only major releases". |
| `$new_version` | `string` | The version WordPress offers. |
| `$current_version` | `string` | The installed version. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_item_types`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the item types, to register types of your own.

A type is a key of lower case letters, digits and underscores, with a label. Invalid
entries are dropped, and core, plugin and theme cannot be removed or renamed away.

Example, register a type for PHP end-of-life warnings:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_item_types',
    function ( $types ) {
        $types['php'] = __( 'PHP', 'my-addon' );
        return $types;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$types` | `array<string, string>` | Type => label. |

Fired in `includes/class-item-types.php`.

### `sc_wpun_notification`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the notification built by the update check, before any channel instance gets its share.

Must return a Notification; anything else is ignored. Each instance then receives the
items of the returned notification that its routing allows.

Example, drop the notes of every item:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_notification',
    function ( $notification ) {
        return $notification->with_items( my_strip_notes( $notification->get_items() ) );
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | The notification, with every item that is waiting. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_plugins_need_update`

*Filter*, since 1.0.0

Filters the plugins that are waiting for an update and will be reported.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$plugins_need_update` | `array<string, object>` | Update data from WordPress by plugin file (for example `hello.php`). |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_should_notify_item`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters whether an item is reported at all, to every channel instance.

An item that is vetoed is not sent and not recorded, but still counts as waiting for an update.

Since 3.0.0 the default is false when the item is muted (see `sc_wpun_mutes()`), so a callback
that returns true whatever it is given unmutes everything. Pass `$notify` on instead.

Example, never report one plugin:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_should_notify_item',
    function ( $notify, $item ) {
        return 'noisy/noisy.php' === $item->get_key() ? false : $notify;
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$notify` | `bool` | Whether to report the item. Default true, false when the item is muted (changed in 3.0.0). |
| `$item` | `Notification_Item` | The item. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_themes_need_update`

*Filter*, since 1.0.0

Filters the themes that are waiting for an update and will be reported.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$themes_need_update` | `array<string, array<string, mixed>>` | Update data from WordPress by theme stylesheet. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_update_items`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the items found by the check, to add, remove or change items.

Runs after core, plugins and themes were collected and before the global settings'
routing. Only Notification_Item objects are kept. An item type other than core,
plugin and theme must be registered with the `sc_wpun_item_types` filter for its
history to be kept up to date: once no item of a registered type is returned,
what was notified about it is forgotten.

Example, report an item of your own:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_update_items',
    function ( $items ) {
        $items[] = new \WPUN\Notification_Item(
            array(
                'type'            => 'php',
                'key'             => 'php',
                'name'            => 'PHP',
                'current_version' => PHP_VERSION,
                'new_version'     => '8.4',
            )
        );
        return $items;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$items` | `Notification_Item[]` | The items found, in the order of the message. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

## Delivery

### `sc_wpun_after_dispatch`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when a round of delivery has finished: a dispatch, or an update check that sent something.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$results` | `array<string, Delivery_Result>` | Result by channel instance id. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | The notification that was delivered. |

Fired in `includes/class-dispatcher.php`, `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_channel_payload`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the payload of any channel just before it is sent.

The shape of the payload is up to the channel; see its documentation. The email
channel uses `array( 'to' => string[], 'subject' => string, 'message' => string, 'headers' => string[] )`.

Example, add a recipient to every email:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_channel_payload',
    function ( $payload, $notification, $instance ) {
        if ( 'email' === $instance->get_type() ) {
            $payload['to'][] = 'archive@example.org';
        }
        return $payload;
    },
    10,
    3
);
```

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$payload` | `mixed` | The payload. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | What is being delivered. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance it is delivered through. |

Fired in `includes/abstract-class-channel.php`.

### `sc_wpun_channel_payload_{type}`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the payload of the channels of one type just before it is sent.

The dynamic part, `$type`, is the channel type, for example `email`. The arguments are the
same as for `sc_wpun_channel_payload`.

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$payload` | `mixed` | The payload. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | What is being delivered. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance it is delivered through. |

Fired in `includes/abstract-class-channel.php`.

### `sc_wpun_email_content`

*Filter*, since 1.4.3. Since 2.0.0 also receives the notification and the instance, and is not HTML-escaped.

Filters the body of the email.

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$body` | `string` | Body: plain text, or HTML if the instance is set to HTML. An HTML body is a fragment: it is wrapped in a document with the language, direction and title after this filter. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | The notification. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance sending it. |

Fired in `includes/class-notifier.php`, `modules/email/class-email-channel.php`.

### `sc_wpun_email_subject`

*Filter*, since 1.4.3. Since 2.0.0 also receives the notification and the instance.

Filters the subject of the email.

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$subject` | `string` | Subject, including the prefix. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | The notification. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance sending it. |

Fired in `includes/class-notifier.php`, `modules/email/class-email-channel.php`.

### `sc_wpun_message_text`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the plain text of a notification, which channels use as the message.

When a length limit is given to the renderer, the filter may run more than once for one message, and the
length is measured on what the filter returns. `$notification` is then a copy with only the items shown
when the message was shortened.

Example, add a line at the end:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_message_text',
    function ( $text, $notification ) {
        return $text . "\n\n-- Sent by my agency";
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$text` | `string` | The plain text. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | The notification it was made from. |
| `$hidden` | `int` | How many items were left out of the text, 0 when none. |

Fired in `includes/class-notification-renderer.php`.

### `sc_wpun_more_items_text`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the line that says how many items were left out of a shortened message.

Return plain text: it is escaped for the format (Markdown, HTML) where needed. The line only exists
when at least one item was left out.

Example, say it in another way:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_more_items_text',
    function ( $text, $hidden ) {
        return sprintf( '(%d more not shown)', $hidden );
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$text` | `string` | The line, for example "…and 3 more". |
| `$hidden` | `int` | How many items were left out. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | The notification, with all its items. |

Fired in `includes/class-notification-renderer.php`.

### `sc_wpun_notification_failed`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when delivering a notification through a channel instance failed.

Also fires for an instance that is switched off or whose channel is not available,
when a delivery to it was asked for.

A result with a `retry_after` defers the instance: update checks skip it until then (at most 7 days).

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$result` | `Delivery_Result` | The result, with the reason in its code and message. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | What was to be delivered. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance. |

Fired in `includes/class-dispatcher.php`.

### `sc_wpun_notification_sent`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when a notification was delivered through a channel instance.

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$result` | `Delivery_Result` | The result. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | What was delivered. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance it was delivered through. |

Fired in `includes/class-dispatcher.php`.

### `sc_wpun_pre_send`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters a delivery before it happens, to replace it with a result of your own.

Return a Delivery_Result to skip the channel and use that result; any other
value sends as normal. Runs for every instance that is switched on and whose
channel is available.

Example, hold all deliveries during maintenance:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_pre_send',
    function ( $pre, $notification, $instance ) {
        return my_maintenance_mode()
            ? \WPUN\Delivery_Result::failure( 'Held back.', 'maintenance' )
            : $pre;
    },
    10,
    3
);
```

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$pre` | `null\|Delivery_Result` | Null. Return a Delivery_Result to short-circuit. |
| `$notification` | `Notification` | What is being delivered. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance it is delivered through. |

Fired in `includes/class-dispatcher.php`.

## Channels and fields

### `sc_wpun_channel_deleted`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires after a channel instance was deleted.

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$id` | `string` | Identifier of the deleted instance. |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The deleted instance. |

Fired in `includes/class-channel-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_channel_fields`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the settings fields of a channel type.

The fields are drawn on the add and edit forms, checked by the default Channel::validate_settings() and can be
supplied from outside the database. Same schema as Channel::get_fields().

A channel that overrides validate_settings() decides for itself what it keeps, so a field added to it here is
drawn but may not be saved. The email channel is one: it keeps only its own fields. Changing the texts of
existing fields is always safe.

Example, change the help text of the email channel's recipients:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_channel_fields',
    function ( $fields, $type ) {
        if ( 'email' === $type && isset( $fields['to'] ) ) {
            $fields['to']['description'] = 'Use the team mailing list.';
        }
        return $fields;
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$fields` | `array<string, array<string, mixed>>` | The field schemas by name. |
| `$type` | `string` | The channel type. |

Fired in `includes/abstract-class-channel.php`.

### `sc_wpun_channel_rejected`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when a channel is refused because the API version of the site does not satisfy what it needs.

Example:

```php
add_action(
    'sc_wpun_channel_rejected',
    function ( $type, $reason, $channel ) {
        error_log( sprintf( 'Channel "%s" was refused: %s', $type, $reason ) );
    },
    10,
    3
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$type` | `string` | The channel type. |
| `$reason` | `string` | Why it was refused, as plain text. |
| `$channel` | `Channel` | The channel that was refused. |

Fired in `includes/class-channel-registry.php`.

### `sc_wpun_channels`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the channel instances defined in code.

Starts with the instances of the `SC_WPUN_CHANNELS` constant. Entries are Channel_Instance objects or
arrays with the keys `id`, `type`, `label`, `enabled`, `settings` and `routing`. An instance defined here
replaces a stored one with the same id, is read-only in the admin and works like any other for delivery.
Invalid entries are reported and skipped.

Example:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_channels',
    function ( $channels ) {
        $channels[] = array(
            'id'       => 'ops_email',
            'type'     => 'email',
            'label'    => 'Operations',
            'enabled'  => true,
            'settings' => array( 'to' => 'ops@example.org' ),
        );
        return $channels;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$channels` | `array<int\|string, Channel_Instance\|array<string, mixed>>` | The instances. |

Fired in `includes/class-channel-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_channels_json`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the JSON text of the `SC_WPUN_CHANNELS` constant, which defines channel instances in code.

Null when the constant is not defined. A filter can supply the JSON itself, for example from a secrets
service. The text is a JSON array of objects with the keys `id`, `type`, `label`, `enabled`, `settings`
and `routing`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$json` | `string\|null` | The JSON text, or null. |

Fired in `includes/class-channel-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_field_types`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the field types the settings screen can draw and settings can be checked with.

The array is keyed by type. Each entry is an array with a `render` and a `sanitize` callable. The built-in
types (`text`, `textarea`, `url`, `email_list`, `secret`, `number`, `boolean` and `enum`) are in it in the
same shape, so an add-on can replace one. `checkbox` and `select` are aliases of `boolean` and `enum`.
An entry that is not an array of two callables is dropped, with a notice to the developer.

`render( $field, $name, $id, $value, $disabled, $described_by, $error )` returns the escaped markup of the
control. `$field` is the field schema, `$name` the `name` attribute, `$id` the `id`, `$value` the current
value, `$disabled` whether the control is read-only and `$described_by` the ids of the elements that
describe it. `$error` is the message of an error to show, or an empty string; the error text itself is
drawn by the caller, so the control only needs to be marked invalid.

For a field with `secret` set, `$value` is `'1'` when a value is saved and `''` when not: the real value is
never passed to the callable.

`sanitize( $value, $field )` returns the clean value, or a WP_Error when the value is not valid. `$field`
is the field schema, with its `name` added. The error is reported against the field.

Example, add a colour type:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_field_types',
    function ( $types ) {
        $types['colour'] = array(
            'render'   => function ( $field, $name, $id, $value ) {
                return '<input type="color" id="' . esc_attr( $id ) . '" name="' . esc_attr( $name ) . '" value="' . esc_attr( $value ) . '" />';
            },
            'sanitize' => function ( $value ) {
                return sanitize_hex_color( $value ) ? sanitize_hex_color( $value ) : new WP_Error( 'invalid_colour', 'Enter a colour.' );
            },
        );
        return $types;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$types` | `array<string, array{render: callable, sanitize: callable}>` | Field types by name. |

Fired in `includes/class-field-types.php`.

### `sc_wpun_register_channels`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when the notification channels are first needed, for modules and add-ons to register theirs.

Example:

```php
add_action(
    'sc_wpun_register_channels',
    function ( \WPUN\Channel_Registry $registry ) {
        $registry->register( new My_Channel() );
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$registry` | `Channel_Registry` | The registry to register channels with. |

Fired in `includes/class-channel-registry.php`.

## Configuration

### `sc_wpun_config_sources`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the configuration sources, in the order they are asked.

The first source to return a value wins. By default constants come first, then environment
variables if enabled. Add your own to read from a secrets service, or reorder the list.
Entries that are not Config_Source objects are dropped.

Example, ask a source of your own after the constants:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_config_sources',
    function ( $sources ) {
        $sources[] = new My_Vault_Source();
        return $sources;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$sources` | `Config_Source[]` | The sources. |

Fired in `includes/class-config.php`.

### `sc_wpun_config_value`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the value of a setting or channel field, the last word before the database is used.

Receives what the configuration sources supplied, or null if none did. Return a value
to override it, or null to use the saved value from the database. Values are scalars
and are cast to the type of the setting or field. Do not log the value: it can be a secret.

Example, take the check frequency from a site option of your own:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_config_value',
    function ( $value, $context, $source ) {
        if ( 'frequency' === $context->get_setting() ) {
            return get_site_option( 'my_frequency', $value );
        }
        return $value;
    },
    10,
    3
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$value` | `string\|bool\|int\|float\|null` | The value the sources supplied, or null. |
| `$context` | `Config_Context` | What is asked for, and the site. |
| `$source` | `string\|null` | Where the value came from, or null. |

Fired in `includes/class-config.php`.

### `sc_wpun_default_settings`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the settings a new install starts with, and the values used for settings that are missing.

Only the keys below are used, and values are cast to the type shown. Anything else
is ignored, as is a return value that is not an array. A notify setting that is not
one of its keys falls back to the built-in default.

Example, check daily by default:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_default_settings',
    function ( $defaults ) {
        $defaults['frequency'] = 'daily';
        return $defaults;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$defaults` | `array<string, mixed>` | The default settings.<br>- `string` `$frequency` Name of a cron schedule.<br>- `string` `$notify_core` `none`, `all` or `major` (major releases only).<br>- `string` `$notify_plugins` `none`, `all` or `active` (active plugins only).<br>- `string` `$notify_themes` `none`, `all` or `active` (active themes only).<br>- `bool` `$hide_updates` True to hide the WordPress update notice from users who cannot update.<br>- `bool` `$download_links` True to add download links to plugin, theme and WordPress items. |

Fired in `includes/class-settings.php`.

### `sc_wpun_get_options_filter`

*Filter*, since 1.4.0

Filters a setting option of the plugin after it is read.

When the plugin runs for a network (see `sc_wpun_is_network()`), the options are network
options, under the same names.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$value` | `mixed` | The stored value. |
| `$field` | `string` | The name of the option. |

Fired in `includes/class-channel-store.php`, `includes/class-mute-store.php`, `includes/class-settings.php`, `includes/class-state.php`.

### `sc_wpun_load_from_env`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters whether configuration is also read from environment variables.

Off unless the environment variable SC_WPUN_LOAD_FROM_ENV is set to an "on" value (1, true,
yes or on), so variables a host happens to set never change the plugin's behaviour by surprise.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$load_from_env` | `bool` | Whether to read environment variables. |

Fired in `includes/class-config.php`.

### `sc_wpun_put_options_filter`

*Filter*, since 1.4.0

Filters a setting option of the plugin before it is stored.

When the plugin runs for a network (see `sc_wpun_is_network()`), the options are network
options, under the same names.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$value` | `mixed` | The value about to be stored. |
| `$field` | `string` | The name of the option. |

Fired in `includes/class-channel-store.php`, `includes/class-mute-store.php`, `includes/class-settings.php`, `includes/class-state.php`.

## Muting

### `sc_wpun_item_muted`

*Action*, since 3.0.0

Fires after an item was muted.

It fires again when a mute is replaced, for example "skip this version" by "always". Use it to log
who muted what, or to keep other sites in step.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$mute` | `Mute` | The mute that was saved. |
| `$source` | `string` | Where the change came from: `plugins_screen`, `settings`, `cli` or `api`. |

Fired in `includes/class-mute-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_item_unmuted`

*Action*, since 3.0.0

Fires after an item was unmuted, or its plugin or theme was deleted.

`$source` is `plugins_screen`, `settings`, `cli` or `api` for an unmute, and `deleted` when the
plugin or theme was deleted.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$previous` | `Mute` | The mute that was removed. |
| `$source` | `string` | Where the change came from. |

Fired in `includes/class-mute-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_mute_capability`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters the capability needed to mute and unmute plugins and themes.

It decides who sees the mute links and bulk actions on the Plugins screen, and who may use them. It
defaults to the capability of the settings page (`sc_wpun_capability`, `manage_options` on a single
site), so a site can let maintainers mute without giving them the whole settings screen. An empty or
non-string value is ignored and the default is used.

The Muted tab is part of the settings page, so seeing it still needs the settings capability, and
its forms need both. WP-CLI and the PHP API are not affected: they do not check capabilities.

Example, let users who can update plugins mute and unmute:

```php
add_filter( 'sc_wpun_mute_capability', fn() => 'update_plugins' );
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$capability` | `string` | Capability. Default is the one `sc_wpun_capability` returns. |

Fired in `includes/admin/class-mute-actions.php`.

### `sc_wpun_mute_ended`

*Action*, since 3.0.0

Fires once when a mute ends while an update is waiting: a "skip this version" mute because a newer
version is offered, or a snooze because its time has passed.

The check records the ended mute in the run state, not in the stored mutes, so the action does
not fire on later runs. It never fires in a dry run. If two checks overlap, it can fire twice;
see ADR 0009. It can also not fire at all: saving or removing any mute drops the ended ones, so
if that happens after the mute ended and before the next check, the end is not reported.
A mute that ended both ways at once is reported once, with `expired`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$mute` | `Mute` | The mute that ended. |
| `$item` | `Notification_Item` | The item that is waiting. |
| `$reason` | `string` | `version` when a newer version ended a "skip this version" mute, `expired` when the time of a snooze passed. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_mute_source_label`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters the name shown for where a mute was set from.

Example, show "Helpdesk" for an add-on's slug:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_mute_source_label',
    function ( $label, $source ) {
        return 'helpdesk' === $source ? __( 'Helpdesk', 'my-plugin' ) : $label;
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$label` | `string` | The label. Empty for an unknown source. |
| `$source` | `string` | The source as stored. |

Fired in `includes/class-mute-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_mutes`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters the mutes, to define mutes in code.

Receives the stored mutes. Add a `WPUN\Mute` to mute an item from code, for example in an
mu-plugin managed by an agency or by Composer. A mute added here applies like a stored one, is
listed with it and is marked as set in code (`Mute::is_from_code()`), and nobody can unmute it
through the store. It replaces a stored mute of the same item. Values that are not a `Mute`, mutes
of the `core` type and mutes of a type that is not registered with `sc_wpun_item_types` are dropped.
When two mutes are for the same item, the later one wins. A stored mute cannot be hidden: one
the returned list leaves out is put back, so use `sc_wpun_should_notify_item` to report an item
that is muted.

A mute can carry an `expires` time (a Unix timestamp) to end by itself, like a snooze, and a
`source` that says where it came from. Once the time has passed the mute counts as ended.

Example, mute a plugin for good:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_mutes',
    function ( $mutes ) {
        $mutes[] = new \WPUN\Mute(
            array(
                'type' => 'plugin',
                'key'  => 'noisy/noisy.php',
            )
        );
        return $mutes;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$mutes` | `Mute[]` | The stored mutes. |

Fired in `includes/class-mute-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_pre_mute`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters a mute before it is saved, to apply a policy.

Receives the mute, or the `WP_Error` that says why it is refused. Return a `WP_Error` to refuse
it; the message is shown on the screen or by WP-CLI. A returned mute must be for the same item,
and a refusal cannot be turned into a mute. Return a changed mute to, for example, cap how long
a mute lasts. A mute whose `expires` has passed is refused, also when the filter made it so.

Example, refuse muting a security plugin:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_pre_mute',
    function ( $mute ) {
        if ( $mute instanceof \WPUN\Mute && 'security/security.php' === $mute->get_key() ) {
            return new \WP_Error( 'my_policy', 'Security updates must be reported.' );
        }
        return $mute;
    }
);
```

Example, cap a snooze at 30 days:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_pre_mute',
    function ( $mute ) {
        $latest = time() + 30 * DAY_IN_SECONDS;
        if ( $mute instanceof \WPUN\Mute && null !== $mute->get_expires() && $mute->get_expires() > $latest ) {
            return new \WPUN\Mute(
                array(
                    'type'    => $mute->get_type(),
                    'key'     => $mute->get_key(),
                    'until'   => $mute->get_until(),
                    'time'    => $mute->get_time(),
                    'user'    => $mute->get_user_id(),
                    'source'  => $mute->get_source(),
                    'expires' => $latest,
                )
            );
        }
        return $mute;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$mute` | `Mute\|WP_Error` | The mute, or the error that refuses it. |
| `$source` | `string` | Where the change came from: `plugins_screen`, `settings`, `cli` or `api`. |

Fired in `includes/class-mute-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_pre_unmute`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters whether a mute may be removed, to apply a policy.

Return a `WP_Error` to refuse; the message is shown on the screen or by WP-CLI. Anything else
than true refuses too. Deleting the plugin or theme removes its mute without asking.

Example, keep the mutes the site's maintainer set:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_pre_unmute',
    function ( $allow, $mute ) {
        return 'maintained/maintained.php' === $mute->get_key() ? new \WP_Error( 'my_policy', 'Ask the maintainer.' ) : $allow;
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$allow` | `true\|WP_Error` | Whether to unmute. Default true. |
| `$mute` | `Mute` | The mute. |
| `$source` | `string` | Where the change came from: `plugins_screen`, `settings`, `cli` or `api`. |

Fired in `includes/class-mute-store.php`.

### `sc_wpun_snooze_durations`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters the lengths of a snooze offered on the Plugins screen, the Muted tab and in WP-CLI.

A list of seconds => label. Entries whose seconds are not a positive whole number or whose label is
not a non-empty string are dropped. Only these lengths are accepted from the Plugins screen links.

Example, offer 4 hours as well:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_snooze_durations',
    function ( $durations ) {
        return array( 4 * HOUR_IN_SECONDS => __( '4 hours', 'my-plugin' ) ) + $durations;
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$durations` | `array<int, string>` | Label by number of seconds. |

Fired in `includes/class-mute-store.php`.

## Settings screen

### `sc_wpun_after_channel_form`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires inside the add and edit form of a channel, after its last section and before the buttons.

On the form of a new channel the instance is a provisional, unsaved one: the id it would get from the
prefilled label, the type, the label of the module, switched off, with the default settings.

Example, add a note:

```php
add_action(
    'sc_wpun_after_channel_form',
    function ( $instance, $channel ) {
        echo '<p>' . esc_html( $instance->get_id() ) . '</p>';
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance being edited, or the provisional one of a new channel. |
| `$channel` | `Channel` | The module of the instance. |

Fired in `includes/admin/class-channel-form.php`.

### `sc_wpun_before_channel_form`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires inside the add and edit form of a channel, before its first section.

Output extra markup here. The plugin does not save extra inputs. On the form of a new channel
the instance is a provisional, unsaved one: the id it would get from the prefilled label, the type,
the label of the module, switched off, with the default settings.

Example, add a note:

```php
add_action(
    'sc_wpun_before_channel_form',
    function ( $instance, $channel ) {
        echo '<p>' . esc_html( $channel->get_label() ) . '</p>';
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

`$instance` holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$instance` | `Channel_Instance` | The instance being edited, or the provisional one of a new channel. |
| `$channel` | `Channel` | The module of the instance. |

Fired in `includes/admin/class-channel-form.php`.

### `sc_wpun_capability`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the capability needed to use the plugin's settings page.

It decides who sees the settings page, saves the settings, sends a test message
and dismisses the plugin's notice. An empty or non-string value is ignored and
the default is used.

The default is `manage_options`, or `manage_network_options` on multisite, which
only super admins have, as with core's update screens.

Lowering it hands every user with the capability control over where the plugin's
notifications go. Such a user can:

- send the update notifications, a list of the site's outdated and possibly
  vulnerable plugins and themes, to any address;
- send test messages to any address;
- change the From and Reply-To addresses;
- add, edit, switch off, duplicate and delete channels;
- hide the core update notice and run the update check on demand;
- see the values of channel settings set in `wp-config.php` or by the environment
  when the field is not secret and its schema sets `show_external`.

Example, let editors manage the plugin:

```php
add_filter( 'sc_wpun_capability', fn() => 'edit_pages' );
```

Network-activated, the screen is in the network admin, which only users who can manage the
network reach, so lowering this to `manage_options` does not let the administrators of the
sites in. Lower it to a capability that users who manage the network have, or leave it.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$capability` | `string` | Capability. Default `manage_options`, or `manage_network_options` on multisite. |

Fired in `includes/admin/class-settings-page.php`.

### `sc_wpun_settings_tab_{tab}`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Draws a tab of the settings screen.

The dynamic part, `$tab`, is the tab's slug. Add the tab with the `sc_wpun_settings_tabs` filter;
it is listed only while something is hooked here. Output inside the screen's wrapper.

Fired in `includes/admin/class-settings-page.php`.

### `sc_wpun_settings_tabs`

*Filter*, since 2.0.0

Filters the tabs of the settings screen.

A tab is shown only if something is hooked on `sc_wpun_settings_tab_{$tab}` to draw it. Entries
whose slug is not a string equal to its `sanitize_key()` form, or whose label is not a string,
are ignored. The General tab cannot be removed.

Example, add a tab:

```php
add_filter( 'sc_wpun_settings_tabs', fn( $tabs ) => $tabs + array( 'mine' => 'Mine' ) );
add_action( 'sc_wpun_settings_tab_mine', fn() => print '<p>Hello</p>' );
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$tabs` | `array<string, string>` | Tab labels keyed by slug. Default `general`, `channels`, `muted` and `about`. The About tab is always moved last, and is hidden by the `show_about` setting (code only). |

Fired in `includes/admin/class-settings-page.php`.

## Lifecycle and legacy

### `sc_wpun_auto_update_enabled`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters whether an update counts as installed automatically, which adds the `auto_update` flag and its note to the item.

The default follows WordPress: automatic updates are on for the item and can run on this site (the
`AUTOMATIC_UPDATER_DISABLED` and `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS` constants, version control checkouts, the
auto-update settings and the `auto_update_*` filters). Use it for an updater outside WordPress that
installs the update later. Returning false removes the flag and the note.

Example, a host that updates plugins itself:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_auto_update_enabled',
    function ( $enabled, $type ) {
        return $enabled || 'plugin' === $type;
    },
    10,
    2
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$enabled` | `bool` | Whether automatic updates are on for the item. |
| `$type` | `string` | `core`, `plugin` or `theme`. |
| `$key` | `string` | `core`, the plugin file or the theme stylesheet. |
| `$new_version` | `string` | The version that is waiting. |

Fired in `includes/class-auto-update-policy.php`.

### `sc_wpun_disable_cron`

*Action*, since 1.0.0

Fires when the plugin is deactivated, to turn the scheduled check off.

Fired in `includes/class-plugin.php`, `includes/class-scheduler.php`.

### `sc_wpun_item_download_url`

*Filter*, since 3.0.0

Filters the address of a download link before it is added to an item, when download links are on.

Not run when the "Download links" setting is off. Return an empty string to leave the link out.
The address comes from the update data and can hold a licence key or a private token.

Example, keep only downloads from WordPress.org:

```php
add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_item_download_url',
    function ( $url ) {
        return 0 === strpos( $url, 'https://downloads.wordpress.org/' ) ? $url : '';
    }
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$url` | `string` | The package address from the update data. |
| `$type` | `string` | Item type: `plugin`, `theme` or `core`. |
| `$key` | `string` | Plugin file, theme stylesheet or `core`. |

Fired in `includes/class-update-checker.php`.

### `sc_wpun_loaded`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Fires when the plugin has loaded and its hooks are registered.

Add-ons can use it as the moment to start talking to the plugin's API.

Fired in `includes/class-plugin.php`.

## Actions you can fire

The plugin listens to these actions but does not fire them itself. Call them with `do_action()`.

### `sc_wpun_enable_cron`

*Action*, since 1.0.0

Schedules the update check. Handled by the `Scheduler` class.

Kept from 1.x. Schedules the check at the saved frequency, unless it is already scheduled at it.
The plugin does this itself on every request (on `init`), so there is rarely a reason to call it.
Pass a frequency to schedule at it instead of the saved one; `manual` stops the checks, as
`sc_wpun_disable_cron` does.

```php
do_action( 'sc_wpun_enable_cron' );
do_action( 'sc_wpun_enable_cron', 'daily' );
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$frequency` | `string` | Optional. A frequency key from `sc_wpun_frequencies`, such as `daily`, or `manual`. Default is the saved frequency. |

Handled in `includes/class-plugin.php`.

### `sc_wpun_run_check`

*Action*, since 2.0.0

Runs the update check now.

It works as a scheduled run does: same routing, per-instance dedupe, delivery state and
hooks, so items an instance was already told about are not sent again. The notification
source is `manual` and the schedule is not changed. Use it from a deploy script. From a
system cron, run `wp updates-notifier check` instead: it has a dry run, a force option and an
exit status.

There is no lock: a run that overlaps another check, scheduled or manual, can send an
update the other is also sending, so it may arrive twice. A channel that must never
deliver twice can keep its own record of what it sent.

```php
do_action( 'sc_wpun_run_check' );
```

There is no capability check. Before firing it from anything a user can reach, check
`current_user_can()` with the capability from the `sc_wpun_capability` filter.

Handled in `includes/class-plugin.php`.
